_readme: Registry for tools/check-scholar-balance.mjs (CLAUDE.md -> READER-IN-THE-PEW RULE, owner-directed 2026-11-24).

It records the ROLE a named scholar usually plays ON THIS SITE, so the tool can count the bench. It is NOT a judgment of anyone's faith: Dunn and James F. McGrath are believing scholars who appear here as dissent from the specific readings our pages defend. How each may be DESCRIBED is governed by docs/scholar-labels.md, not by this file.
defenders = scholars whose work our positive case is built on. dissenters = scholars who appear as the objection or the dissent. mixed = named either way, counted for neither.
A dissenter mentioned in a sentence where he CONCEDES a fact (see witnessCues) is counted as a hostile witness, which counts for the case, not against it.

Each entry: name (for the report) + pattern (a case-sensitive JS regex source, tested against plain text). Keep patterns narrow enough not to hit a first name or a place (Craig Keener, Bruce Metzger, the country France).
Add a scholar here in the same change that first names him on the site. Naming a new DEFENDER on a page still needs apologia-citations: this file counts names, it does not verify them.

defenders.name: Raymond E. Brown
defenders.note: SCOPE: a defender of the point that the two infancy narratives independently AGREE on the virginal conception (Birth of the Messiah, 34-37, 517). NOT a defender of its historicity by historical method (he judged that unresolved), nor of the family-memoir sourcing. See docs/scholar-labels.md.

mixed.name: Samuel Sandmel
mixed.note: The Jewish scholar whose 'parallelomania' caution (1961) our typology pages ADOPT as a control on their own method. He was not writing against Christian typology, so he is not counted as dissent.

mixed.name: John A. T. Robinson
mixed.note: A liberal Anglican bishop (Honest to God) whose Redating the New Testament (1976) argued the whole New Testament was written before AD 70. Theologically liberal and 'no friend of conservative apologetics' (library/earlydate.html); cited for that case only, so counted for neither side.

mixed.name: Paula Fredriksen
mixed.note: Mixed by default: she holds that Jesus was hailed as Messiah before Easter and died under the title (against Wrede), but doubts he publicly claimed it. Where a page makes her its named objection, record her under unitRoles.dissenter for that page.

mixed.name: Ulrich Luz
mixed.note: Cited for the distinction between a 'miracle secret' and a 'messianic secret' in Mark (ZNW 56, 1965), which our reply to Wrede uses. NOT a defender of a historical origin for the secrecy, nor of Jesus's messianic claim — so he is counted for neither side (neutrality + pastor lenses, 2026-11-24). Never say he 'argued against Wrede'.

unitRoles._readme: Per-card / per-essay role corrections, each with a written reason. 'witness' lists scholars from the dissenters list who, ON THIS PAGE, argue FOR the claim the page defends — so every mention of them there is a hostile witness, not dissent. Use sparingly: a wrong entry hides real dissent.
unitRoles._readme_defender: 'defender' lists scholars from the dissenters list whom THIS page names as answering the objection — a believing scholar who dissents on one question may defend our reading on another. Same caution: a wrong entry hides real dissent.
unitRoles._readme_dissenter: 'dissenter' lists scholars from the MIXED list who are the named objection on THIS page, so they count as dissent there. Added 2026-11-24 after the pastor lens caught the count on arg-jesus-messiah-claim leaving out its headline critic.

ev-s3.html#arg-jesus-messiah-claim.why: On Wrede's messianic-secret theory Dunn argued AGAINST Wrede — that the secrecy in Mark has a historical rather than a purely theological origin (library/jesus-messiah-claim.html, footnote 14, 'The Messianic Secret in Mark'). He is this card's named reply to Wrede, not a dissenter from it. Paula Fredriksen is the card's second named objection, with a section of her own ('He never plainly said it' — stated fairly, where she is named in the first sentence), so she counts as dissent here.

ev-s3.html#arg-hist_jesus.why: On the existence of Jesus both men wrote whole books AGAINST mythicism (Ehrman, Did Jesus Exist?, 2012; Casey, Jesus: Evidence and Argument or Mythicist Myths?, 2014). Here they are the page's star non-Christian witnesses, not its critics.

library/hist_jesus.html.why: Same reason as the card: on this essay's question both argue for Jesus's existence against the mythicists.
